title: 7 Best Sales Operations Software Tools for 2026
summary: Compare seven of the best sales operations software tools for CRM, forecasting, planning, commissions, analytics, and sales engagement.
body_markdown:
Sales operations software helps teams manage the systems and processes behind selling, from customer data and forecasting to planning, compensation, analytics, and sales engagement.


Sales operations isn’t one tool but a stack of five jobs, and this guide names the best tool per job: customer relationship management (Salesforce and HubSpot Sales Hub), sales forecasting (Clari), territory, quota, and commission management (CaptivateIQ), sales analytics and revenue intelligence (Gong), and sales engagement (Salesloft and Outreach).


In this article, we compare the top seven sales operations tools by category, including the job each is best for, the evidence behind the pick, and an honest caveat. CaptivateIQ is our platform and anchors the compensation and planning category. Every rating cited in this guide is published by G2.


## What’s the Difference Between Sales Operations and Revenue Operations?


Sales operations manages the systems and processes that support sales organizations, including forecasting, territories, quotas, compensation, and pipeline analytics.


Revenue operations (RevOps) has a broader scope, coordinating operations across marketing, sales, and customer success. A[RevOps software](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/revops-software) stack includes the systems, data, and workflows shared across those functions, while sales operations can sit within the larger RevOps function.

## The 7 Best Sales Operations Software Tools by Category


The seven tools below are organized by the sales operations job they’re designed to support. Each review covers what the tool does, where it fits best, supporting evidence, and one limitation to consider.


### Category: Customer Relationship Management (CRM)


CRM software gives sales operations a central system of record for accounts, contacts, opportunities, and sales activity. When an organization lacks a reliable CRM system, forecasting, analytics, planning, and other sales operations functions have incomplete or inconsistent information to work from.


#### 1. Salesforce


**Best for:** Enterprise CRM and centralized sales data


Salesforce’s sales product, now branded as[Agentforce Sales](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/) (formerly Sales Cloud), is a CRM platform that centralizes leads, accounts, opportunities, activity, and reporting while supporting automation and integrations with the rest of the sales technology stack.


Salesforce gives sales operations teams a single source of truth, which helps keep data consistent across connected sales systems.


The platform has a[4.4 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/agentforce-sales-formerly-salesforce-sales-cloud/reviews) across roughly 25,900 reviews, the largest review base of any tool on this list. Its tradeoffs are administration and complexity. Salesforce’s learning curve is its top “cons” theme on G2, with more than 1,000 mentions, so teams planning to use it should account for the expertise and time required to configure and maintain the system.


Salesforce publishes multiple product tiers on its current[sales pricing page](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/pricing/) .


#### 2. HubSpot Sales Hub


**Best for:** Mid-market teams that want CRM plus automation without an admin team


[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/sales) combines CRM data with sales automation, prospecting, pipeline management, and reporting. Sales Hub is built on HubSpot Smart CRM, giving sales operations teams a central place to manage customer records while providing reps and managers with tools for day-to-day sales work.


The HubSpot setup gives mid-market teams CRM and common sales workflows in one product without necessarily requiring a dedicated CRM administrator.


HubSpot Sales Hub has a[4.4 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/hubspot-sales-hub/reviews) across roughly 13,900 reviews. Ease of use is its top-mentioned strength, with more than 1,200 mentions. G2 lists missing features as the top “cons” tag, and reviewers note that some advanced customization and automation capabilities are limited to higher-tier plans.


HubSpot publishes its available tiers on the[Sales Hub pricing page](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/sales) .


### Category: Sales Forecasting


Sales forecasting software turns CRM and deal data into revenue projections that help operations teams track performance against targets. If a company doesn’t use sales forecasting software, leadership may have to rely on disconnected spreadsheets, stale CRM fields, or subjective deal estimates.


#### 3. Clari


**Best for:** Forecast calls and pipeline inspection at enterprise scale


[Clari](https://www.clari.com/) is a revenue forecasting platform that gives sales operations and leadership teams a shared view of forecasts, pipeline changes, and deal risk.


Clari Forecast combines historical deal data with current sales activity and supports forecast rollups, scenario modeling, and drill-downs from top-line forecasts to individual deals. Visibility into historical deal data and forecast changes gives teams a structured way to inspect the pipeline before and during forecast calls.


Clari also shows sales operations teams why the forecast moved. Teams can trace changes back to individual opportunities and keep forecast calls focused on the deals and assumptions behind the current projection instead of assembling updates by hand.


Clari has a[4.6 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/clari/reviews) across roughly 5,600 reviews. Forecasting is a top-mentioned strength with 486 mentions, and G2 reports an average implementation time of two months.


The main caveats to Clari relate to customization and data alignment. G2 reviewers flag limited customization, and because Clari depends on CRM data, teams need to keep it aligned with Salesforce or another source CRM for forecasts and deal insights to remain useful.


Clari and Salesloft[now operate as one](https://www.salesloft.com/company/newsroom/salesloft-unveils-unified-brand-identity) following their merger.


### Category: Territory, Quota, and Commission Management


Territory, quota, and commission management software[connects account coverage and rep targets](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/headcount-planning) to the compensation plans that pay against those targets. Without territory, quota, and commission management software, changes to assignments or targets can create manual reconciliation work, compensation conflicts, and delays in carrying new plans through to payouts.


#### 4. CaptivateIQ


**Best for:** Connecting territories, quotas, and commissions in one platform so plan changes recalculate pay automatically


[CaptivateIQ](https://www.captivateiq.com/) is a sales performance management platform that connects territory and quota planning with incentive compensation.[CaptivateIQ Planning](https://www.captivateiq.com/planning) supports territory carving, quota setting, capacity modeling, and scenario planning, while[CaptivateIQ Incentives](https://www.captivateiq.com/incentives) handles commission calculations and compensation plan management.[SmartGrid](https://www.captivateiq.com/smartgrid) , its no-code calculation engine, supports complex compensation logic and modeling, while what-if scenarios let teams evaluate changes before putting them into effect.


Connecting planning and compensation is important because a quota change isn’t finished when a new target appears in a planning model. The platform can sync quota changes with incentive structures, allowing planning decisions to carry through to compensation without teams manually rebuilding the same change in a separate system. For a closer look at tools focused on the planning side of the process, see our guide to[sales territory planning software](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/territory-planning-software-2026) .


Automation remains an industry-wide challenge. According to CaptivateIQ’s[2026 State of Incentive Compensation research](https://www.captivateiq.com/blog/state-of-incentive-compensation-2026) , only 33% of organizations have fully automated their commission process. For sales operations teams, an automation gap often starts when territory and quota changes have to be carried manually into compensation. Connecting planning and incentives lets those changes flow through without the same manual handoffs.


CaptivateIQ has a[4.7 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/captivateiq/reviews) across roughly 3,500 reviews, with ease of use cited more than 500 times. One enterprise compensation administrator reported[reducing commission processing from 20 days to six](https://www.g2.com/products/captivateiq/reviews/captivateiq-review-12495742) after using CaptivateIQ.


Some G2 reviewers want more flexibility in ad hoc reporting, particularly when building highly specific reports outside their standard reporting needs.


### Category: Sales Analytics and Revenue Intelligence


Sales analytics and revenue intelligence software capture signals from deals and customer conversations that may not appear in structured CRM fields. Teams missing sales analytics and revenue intelligence software can see reported deal stages and values but remain blind to underlying deal risks and declining engagement.


#### 5. Gong


**Best for:** Conversation intelligence and deal-risk analytics


[Gong](https://www.gong.io/) is a revenue intelligence platform that captures and analyzes sales conversations, including calls and meetings. Its conversation intelligence capabilities record, transcribe, and analyze interactions. Gong uses activity and conversation data to help teams identify risk inside active opportunities, including cases where the recorded stage looks healthy but engagement or deal activity suggests otherwise.


Gong has a[4.7 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/gong/reviews) across roughly 6,700 reviews. Reviewers frequently praise its ease of use for reviewing calls and surfacing actionable conversation insights, and G2 reports an average implementation time of one month.


Transcription accuracy can decline when conversations contain specialized terminology. G2 reviewers have reported errors involving technical vocabulary, abbreviations, and product-specific language, which can require manual verification.


### Category: Sales Engagement


Sales engagement software organizes sequences, calls, emails, and follow-up tasks so reps can execute outreach consistently at scale. In environments that operate without sales engagement software, outreach can depend on individual rep habits, making activity harder for sales ops to measure and coordinate across the team.


#### 6. Salesloft


**Best for:** Structured sales engagement workflows


[Salesloft](https://www.salesloft.com/) is a sales engagement platform built around structured workflows for prospecting and follow-up. Sales sequences organize calls, emails, and other touches into repeatable workflows, while automation helps sales teams manage activity across larger prospect lists.


Because reps work from the same sequences, sales operations can compare how teams are following the outreach process instead of trying to make sense of rep-created follow-up routines. Sales operations can then spot where activity drops off or where the outreach process needs adjustment.


Salesloft has a[4.5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/salesloft/reviews) across roughly 4,300 reviews. Ease of use is its top-mentioned strength with 569 mentions, and G2 reports an average implementation time of one month. G2 reviewers note that the platform can feel overwhelming for new users learning its features and workflows.


#### 7. Outreach


**Best for:** Enterprise engagement with heavier forecasting and deal-management ambitions


‍[Outreach](https://www.outreach.io/) combines sales engagement with capabilities for pipeline management, deal management, conversation intelligence, and forecasting. Teams can use sequences to structure outreach, while managers use the broader platform to inspect activity and opportunities.


Outreach has a[4.3 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/outreach/reviews) across roughly 3,600 reviews, and G2 reports an average implementation time of one month. Its 4.3 rating is the lowest among the seven tools on this list.


Its breadth can make Outreach feel heavier than necessary for teams that mainly need engagement workflows. Some G2 reviewers cite a learning curve, limited customization, or interface complexity among their concerns.


## How to Choose Sales Operations Software


Start with the process that’s creating the most operational friction, then evaluate how the new tool will exchange data with the rest of your stack. Use the following three questions to guide your decision.


### 1. Which Sales Operations Job Needs the Most Attention?


Match the problem you’re trying to solve to the software category designed to handle it:


- **CRM software** addresses customer and opportunity data.


- **Forecasting software** helps teams predict how much revenue they expect to close.


- **Planning and commission software** manages territories, quotas, and pay.


- **Revenue intelligence** software adds deal and conversation signals.


- **Sales engagement software** organizes outreach and follow-up.


### 2. How Will Data Move Between Systems?


Check whether changes to account, rep, and target data flow automatically between the CRM, territory and quota planning, and compensation systems. If teams have to update the same information manually in multiple systems, mismatches can lead to incorrect assignments, quotas, or payouts. The ideal setup keeps that data synchronized across systems as changes happen.


### 3. How Much Implementation Work Can the Team Absorb?


Implementation time varies, even across established platforms. Among the tools on this list with G2 implementation data, average implementation times range from one to three months.


Factor the following implementation requirements into your decision:


- Configuration
- Integrations
- Data cleanup
- Training
- Ongoing administration


Teams also need to decide who will own the software after launch and how much technical or vendor support that person will need for routine changes. A system that requires outside help whenever a territory, quota, workflow, or CRM field changes can create a bottleneck after implementation.


Identify which system owns each important piece of data before adding another tool to the stack. If the CRM owns account and opportunity records while another platform owns quotas or compensation logic, determine how changes move between them and how quickly each system updates.


Consider reporting requirements, too. Teams that need to combine information from several systems should understand where that analysis will happen and how the underlying data gets there.


## FAQs


### What software do sales operations teams use?


Sales operations teams typically use CRM, sales forecasting, territory, quota, and commission management software, sales analytics and revenue intelligence software, and sales engagement software. Common options include Salesforce or HubSpot for CRM, Clari for forecasting, CaptivateIQ for territories, quotas, and commissions, Gong for revenue intelligence, and Salesloft or Outreach for sales engagement.


### What is the best sales operations software?


The best sales operations software depends on the problem your team needs to solve. If customer data is inconsistent, Salesforce or HubSpot can help. If forecasts are unreliable, Clari improves forecasting visibility. CaptivateIQ addresses disconnected planning and commissions, Gong surfaces buyer activity and deal risk, and Salesloft and Outreach help teams standardize inconsistent outreach and follow-up.


### What does a sales operations team do?


A sales operations team manages the systems, data, processes, and planning that help a sales organization execute. Responsibilities can include CRM administration, forecasting, territory design, quota setting, incentive compensation, sales analytics, reporting, and sales technology management. The exact scope varies by company size and organizational structure.


### Is sales operations the same as RevOps?


No. Sales operations focuses on the systems and processes supporting the sales organization, such as forecasting, territories, quotas, compensation, and analytics. Revenue operations has a wider scope that coordinates operations across marketing, sales, and customer success, including the systems and data shared across those functions.


### How much does sales operations software cost?


Sales operations software pricing varies by category, company size, user count, and feature requirements. Many enterprise tools on this list use custom pricing, while Salesforce publishes[sales product tiers](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/pricing/) and HubSpot publishes[Sales Hub tiers](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/sales) . Check vendor pricing pages directly when budgeting because packaging and prices can change.
